title: The Potential of AI Chatbots in Enhancing Lesson Planning in K-12 Education - Insights from Practicum-Experienced Teaching Graduate Students
extended_summary:
This thesis examines whether and how generative AI chatbots support lesson planning for teacher candidates preparing to teach in K-12 settings. The paper asks three main questions: the extent to which preservice teachers use AI chatbots during practicum, the benefits and challenges they experience, and their views on school-age students using these tools. The motivation is to understand a rapidly emerging educational use case for generative AI, particularly for instructional planning, curriculum development, feedback, and related preparation tasks.

The study uses a mixed-methods design combining an anonymous survey and semi-structured interviews. The survey was distributed to Master of Teaching program students and yielded 103 valid responses; four respondents were also interviewed. Participants were graduate-level teacher candidates with practicum experience in K-12 classrooms in Ontario, Canada. Most reported using AI chatbots, especially ChatGPT, for generating lesson ideas, creating activities, and drafting feedback, with use occurring occasionally to about half the time for many respondents.

The main conclusion is that teacher candidates generally perceived AI chatbots as useful for increasing efficiency and improving lesson quality, but they also identified important concerns. Reported issues included technical problems, over-reliance on AI, privacy and data security, intellectual property concerns, potential bias, and alignment with curriculum standards. The thesis argues that AI can be a helpful instructional support, but only if used critically and with ethical oversight, professional guidance, and clear boundaries to avoid harmful dependence or pedagogical misalignment.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI generative AI chatbot/large language model used for text-based conversational assistance, content generation, and response drafting.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as one of the AI chatbots used by practicum-experienced K-12 teacher candidates for lesson planning, generating lesson ideas, creating activities, and providing feedback on student work during practicum.

findings.finding_summary: Among 103 valid survey responses, 78% reported using AI chatbots for lesson planning during practicum, and ChatGPT was the most commonly used tool (79% of chatbot users). Participants reported that it helped them generate lesson content ideas, classroom discussion prompts, lesson materials, and feedback on student work, and many perceived it as improving efficiency and lesson quality.
findings.measure: Survey-reported use of AI chatbots for lesson planning and perceived benefits of ChatGPT in lesson preparation

findings.finding_summary: Some participants raised concerns about over-reliance on AI, technical issues, privacy and data security, intellectual theft, bias/fairness, and alignment with curriculum standards. The thesis also notes risks of diminished critical thinking and pedagogical misalignment when chatbots are used uncritically.
findings.measure: Survey and interview reports of concerns and challenges associated with AI chatbot use

identified_tools.name: Magic School AI
identified_tools.description: An education-focused generative AI platform designed to support teachers with lesson-planning and classroom materials.
identified_tools.use_case: Included as one of the AI chatbots reportedly used by practicum-experienced K-12 teacher candidates for lesson planning, though at a much lower rate than ChatGPT.

findings.finding_summary: The survey reported that 9% of participants who used AI chatbots indicated using Magic School AI. The paper groups it with other chatbots that were used to generate lesson ideas, activities, and teaching materials to save time and support lesson planning.
findings.measure: Self-reported chatbot usage in lesson planning

identified_tools.name: Eduaide.AI
identified_tools.description: An education-focused AI platform for generating lesson plans, presentations, quizzes, and other instructional materials.
identified_tools.use_case: Reported as one of the chatbot tools used by K-12 practicum teacher candidates for lesson planning and curriculum support.

findings.finding_summary: The survey reported that 5% of participants who used AI chatbots indicated using Eduaide.AI. It was used in the broader set of tools for creating lesson ideas, materials, and feedback supports, which participants perceived as efficient and helpful for teaching preparation.
findings.measure: Self-reported chatbot usage in lesson planning

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI chatbots/large language model systems used for conversational assistance, content generation, and instructional support without a single named product focus.
identified_tools.use_case: The thesis frames the study broadly around generative AI chatbots in K-12 lesson planning, especially when discussing benefits, challenges, ethics, and teacher candidates' experiences with multiple tools.

findings.finding_summary: Across 103 valid survey responses, 78% reported using AI chatbots for lesson planning during practicum, and 25.33% used them about half the time while 18.67% used them most of the time and 2.67% always. Participants commonly used chatbots to generate lesson content ideas (46%), facilitate classroom discussions (20%), provide feedback on student work (10%), and assist with homework (14%).
findings.measure: Self-reported frequency and applications of generative AI chatbot use for lesson planning

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported concerns about over-reliance on AI, diminished critical thinking, privacy and data security, intellectual theft, bias and fairness, and alignment with curriculum standards. The paper also notes that some nonusers avoided the tools because of skepticism, budget constraints, lack of knowledge, or concerns about effectiveness and poor-quality AI-generated answers.
findings.measure: Survey and interview reports of challenges, non-use reasons, and ethical concerns

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods thesis with survey and interview data, which provides useful primary evidence but not experimental causal identification. The evidence is qualitative/observational and based on self-report, so it fits a yellow tier rather than higher-evidence categories.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear perceived benefits and substantial adoption, but it does not provide effect sizes or objective outcome gains. It also reports meaningful concerns and mixed/negative issues such as over-reliance, privacy, and poor-quality answers, so overall impact is unclear rather than clearly large or modest.
